content.text:
What kind of story is The Three Billy Goats Gruff?

The Three Billy Goats Gruff is the story of three goats who must cross a bridge to reach a green meadow, and the monstrous troll that lurks beneath it. The repeating structure of each goat crossing in turn, from smallest to largest, and the ending where cleverness defeats the troll make it a thrill.

content.alt: The Three Billy Goats Gruff - The original story of The Three Billy Goats Gruff
content.text:
The original story of The Three Billy Goats Gruff

The original is the Norwegian folk tale "Three Billy Goats Gruff," collected in the 19th century by Asbjørnsen and Moe. Its heart lies in the trip-trap of hooves crossing the bridge, the troll's threats, and the satisfying ending in which the biggest goat drives the troll away.

content.alt: The Three Billy Goats Gruff - Three Billy Goats Gruff story summary
content.text:
Three Billy Goats Gruff story summary

To reach the grass, the goats must cross a bridge where a troll lives. The little goat and the middle goat cleverly get past the troll by saying "A bigger brother is coming soon," and at last the biggest, strongest goat firmly defeats the troll, so all three can eat their fill in the green meadow.
content.caption: Abundance brought by wisdom

content.alt: The Three Billy Goats Gruff - The lesson of The Three Billy Goats Gruff
content.text:
The lesson of The Three Billy Goats Gruff

The core message is to think wisely even in a scary situation, and to be brave when it counts. Talk with your child about how even a small strength, through taking turns and working together, can overcome a big difficulty.

content.alt: The Three Billy Goats Gruff - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Make the trip-trap sound of crossing the bridge grow louder and louder (from the little goat to the big goat). The troll fierce, the ending triumphant! Ask "How could we get past the troll?" to let your child come up with clever ideas. Best suited for ages 3 to 6.
content.caption: A story enjoyed through sound

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Three Billy Goats Gruff good for?
A. Best suited for ages 3 to 6. The repeating structure and the ever-louder sounds are fun for younger children.

Q. Won't the troll be scary?
A. In versions for young children the troll is drawn comically and the ending is satisfying, so kids can enjoy it with peace of mind.

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Stomping feet to make bridge-crossing sounds, playing with goat dolls in different sizes, and role-playing "getting past with wisdom" all work great.
